chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: John Tumino, the Century Room, the big band and Don Robey's tours
summary: Tumino co-owned and booked the band, leased the Century Room, bought uniforms; Don Robey booked tours in Texas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Tumino now was what? The owner of Martin's?
No, John Tumino was like a co-owner, with McShann, of the band. And he was our booking agent.

And he leased this club called the Century Room.
They bought us some fine uniforms, black coats and -- what you that the men wear, call those striped pants, like evening dress, Gamble, waistells,4le striped trousers. And made a good appearance. And McShann did pretty good there.
But in the meantime, Johnny was booking those tours. There was some man down in Houston who actually was running all those tours. He was something -- Ash, or something like that. Ashby?
Anyway, Johnny stayed in contact with him, and he booked us down into those things. So the man had for us - made arrangements to book us into that area.
This was still the small group?
No, this is after -- when we went into the Century Room, he enlarged.
Oh, this is (inaudible) -- you enlarged there to get a big band.

Yeah, this is the latter part of 1939. Maybe it might have been even the first of 1940. I know it was winter time. And we went down to Wichita and we'd come back, we'd play, and we'd go back to Wichita. But this man booked this thing for us -- Don Robey is the name. And he booked us all the way down to --
That's the name I said, and you laughed.
I thought you said, 'Ramey,' you know. (laughs)
Don Robey, I said. Yeah, he's the man who had the record companies down there later.
That's right. And so he booked us down in -- McShann really actually just tore it up all over that country, you know.
